names: Factory App client on a BYOM Droid Computer
Factory App client on a managed Droid Computer

sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `factory-droids`
- Canonical name: Factory Droids (`claim-factory-droids-identity`)
- Vendor/platform versus surface: Factory is the vendor platform; Droid/Droids is the named agent surface on that platform. This dossier keeps one project id and does not invent a second product id (`claim-factory-droids-sf-identity-family`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-vendor`).
- Current status: actively shipped; checked changelog latest is v0.195.0 dated 2026-08-13 (`claim-factory-droids-sf-status`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-version`).
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-14 (`claim-factory-droids-sf-canonical-url`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-repository-url`).

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: Factory's AI coding agent. Given a natural-language task it plans, writes, tests, and ships code (`claim-factory-droids-sf-what-it-is`). The CLI page presents the same Factory runtime through the interactive terminal, Missions, and headless exec (`claim-factory-droids-sf-architecture`). The Factory App page says local, web, and mobile review surfaces connect to that same runtime (`claim-factory-droids-sf-architecture-app`).
- What it is not: not an open-source runtime. The first-party repo is all-rights-reserved, and Product Terms license proprietary Factory Software plus the Factory Platform SaaS (`claim-factory-droids-sf-not-open-source`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-license-terms`). It is not a second product id from Factory the company (`claim-factory-droids-sf-identity-family`).

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` by inference from first-party runtime/loop docs (`claim-factory-droids-sf-primary-type`).
- Agent-loop owner: Droid owns the model-tool and session harness; the selected model supplies reasoning (`claim-factory-droids-sf-agent-loop-owner`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-loop-local`).
- Architecture: CLI docs describe the same Factory runtime through an interactive terminal UI, Missions, and headless exec (`claim-factory-droids-sf-architecture`). The Factory App page says local/web/mobile review surfaces share that runtime (`claim-factory-droids-sf-architecture-app`). Missions are a documented orchestration layer (`claim-factory-droids-sf-secondary-orchestrator`). Droid Computers are execution locations, not a second official-docs runtime sentence; the one-id / not-a-second-primary-type boundary is inference (`claim-factory-droids-sf-execution-location`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-execution-location-local`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-identity-family`).

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-factory-droids-cli-interactive`, `surface-factory-droids-cli-exec`, `surface-factory-droids-desktop`, `surface-factory-droids-web`, `surface-factory-droids-slack`, `surface-factory-droids-vscode`, `surface-factory-droids-jetbrains`, `surface-factory-droids-zed`, `surface-factory-droids-sdk-typescript`, `surface-factory-droids-sdk-python`, `surface-factory-droids-public-api`, `surface-factory-droids-github-actions`, `surface-factory-droids-remote-client-managed`, `surface-factory-droids-remote-client-byom`, `surface-factory-droids-vendor-relay`.
- Execution location: same-device local CLI (`claim-factory-droids-sf-execution-location-local`); user-controlled BYOM machine or Factory-managed Droid Computer (`claim-factory-droids-sf-execution-location`).

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: Factory-managed catalog (`claim-factory-droids-sf-model-strategy`); Factory Router/Auto Model (`claim-factory-droids-sf-factory-router`); CLI BYOK custom models (`claim-factory-droids-sf-byok`).
- Auth strategy: SAML/OIDC SSO via WorkOS or passwordless magic-link for people; service-account Factory API keys for automation; OAuth login is documented on the security page (`claim-factory-droids-sf-auth-strategy`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-auth-oauth`).
- Provider support: Factory-managed Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, and Droid Core catalog (`claim-factory-droids-sf-provider-support`). BYOK OpenAI/Anthropic/generic providers and local Ollama/LM Studio endpoints are on the BYOK page (`claim-factory-droids-sf-byok`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-local-models`).

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: AGENTS.md and compatible instruction files load as coding guidelines (`claim-factory-droids-sf-context-behavior`).
- Memory: the product page claims knowledge persists across tools and platforms; a separate persistent-memory store is not documented beyond that claim plus session sync (`claim-factory-droids-sf-memory`).
- Compaction: automatic compaction settings; `/compress` on the CLI quickstart; a PreCompact hook on the hooks page (`claim-factory-droids-sf-compaction`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-compaction-compress`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-compaction-precompact`).
- Session behavior: `cloudSessionSync` defaults to true (`claim-factory-droids-sf-session-behavior`); CLI `/sessions` and `/fork` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-session-list-fork`); `droid exec --session-id` and `--fork` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-session-resume-exec`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-session-fork-exec`).

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: Read, LS, Grep, Glob, Create, Edit, ApplyPatch, Execute, WebSearch, FetchUrl, Task, and MCP tools (`claim-factory-droids-sf-tools`). Linear is a first-party issue integration, not a tool-loop replacement (`claim-factory-droids-sf-linear`).
- Extensions: VS Code Marketplace extension plus JetBrains/Zed ACP; plugins package skills, commands, droids, hooks, and MCP servers (`claim-factory-droids-sf-extensions`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-plugins`).
- MCP: stdio, HTTP, and legacy SSE with `/mcp` and `droid mcp` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-mcp`).
- Skills: SKILL.md workflows across project, personal, plugin, mission, and built-in scopes (`claim-factory-droids-sf-skills`).
- Hooks: lifecycle shell hooks in hooks.json (`claim-factory-droids-sf-hooks`).
- APIs: JSON-RPC `droid exec` plus TypeScript/Python SDKs (`claim-factory-droids-sf-api`); public HTTP API (`claim-factory-droids-sf-api-http`).

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: Factory Missions plan then Mission Control; Droid Exec Mission Mode names workers and validators; custom droids (`worker`, `explorer`, and user-defined) via the Task tool (`claim-factory-droids-sf-orchestration`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-orchestration-mission-mode`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-subagents`).
- Parallelism: concurrent or background Task subagents (`claim-factory-droids-sf-parallelism`); isolated `droid exec --worktree` jobs (`claim-factory-droids-sf-parallelism-worktree`).

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: optional OS sandbox (`sandbox.enabled`); default mode is per-command. This is not sandbox-by-default (`claim-factory-droids-sf-isolation`).
- Permissions: Autonomy Level Off/Low/Medium/High with allow/deny/block lists (`claim-factory-droids-sf-permissions`); interactive default `sessionDefaultSettings.autonomyLevel` is off (`claim-factory-droids-sf-permissions-default-off`). `droid exec` is separately read-only by default (`claim-factory-droids-sf-exec-readonly-default`).
- Security: project-scoped writes, command approval, Droid Shield, optional sandbox, SSO/governance. The marketing page also says "secure by default"; that claim is kept beside the optional-sandbox docs (`claim-factory-droids-sf-security`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-secure-by-default-marketing`).
- Data path: files stay on the host filesystem; prompts go to configured providers or gateways; Factory says it does not keep a static repo copy. Cloud session sync can mirror conversations when enabled (`claim-factory-droids-sf-data-path`).

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
List each surface from `surfaces.jsonl` separately. Keep native mobile, first-party mobile web, first-party messaging, vendor relay, remote client, private-network, Termux/mobile terminal, and generic remote shell routes distinct.

- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Local CLI: `surface-factory-droids-cli-interactive`, `surface-factory-droids-cli-exec` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-cli`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-exec`).
  - Desktop: `surface-factory-droids-desktop` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-desktop`). Mac/Windows download targets are a separate claim (`claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-desktop-platforms`).
  - Web: `surface-factory-droids-web` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-web`).
  - First-party mobile web: no distinct surface row. Docs mention mobile review surfaces sharing session context, and a product post claims phone/tablet review and session start; whether `app.factory.ai` on a phone is a dedicated mobile-web UI is unknown (`claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-mobile-web`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-mobile-phone-tablet`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-mobile-access`).
  - Messaging: `surface-factory-droids-slack` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-slack`). README also lists Teams; no first-party Teams install path was opened (`claim-factory-droids-sf-teams-readme`).
  - IDE: `surface-factory-droids-vscode`, `surface-factory-droids-jetbrains`, `surface-factory-droids-zed` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-ide`). Product page names Vim; IDE docs treat other editors as CLI-in-terminal (`claim-factory-droids-sf-product-page-interfaces`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-other-editors-cli`).
  - API/automation: `surface-factory-droids-sdk-typescript`, `surface-factory-droids-sdk-python`, `surface-factory-droids-public-api`, `surface-factory-droids-github-actions` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-sdk`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-api`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-github-actions`).
  - Remote client: `surface-factory-droids-remote-client-managed`, `surface-factory-droids-remote-client-byom` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-remote-client`).
  - Vendor relay: `surface-factory-droids-vendor-relay` (`claim-factory-droids-sf-surface-vendor-relay`).
  - Private-network, generic remote shell, and terminal-on-mobile: unknown. No first-party surface rows.
- Remote behavior: Factory App or Slack can start work on a Droid Computer; BYOM traffic uses Factory relay (`claim-factory-droids-sf-remote-access`).
- Mobile behavior: phone/tablet review and session start are first-party claims; native app installers are unknown (`claim-factory-droids-sf-mobile-access`).
- Background behavior: scheduled/Slack/GitHub automations; `droid exec`; `Factory-AI/droid-action`; background Task subagents (`claim-factory-droids-sf-background`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-background-exec`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-background-action`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-background-subagents`).

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: Pro $20/mo, Plus $100/mo, Max $200/mo; Business and Enterprise are contact-sales. Individual usage uses rolling rate limits, then Droid Core, then Extra Usage (`claim-factory-droids-sf-pricing`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-pricing-usage`).
- License: all-rights-reserved repository plus proprietary Product Terms (`claim-factory-droids-sf-not-open-source`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-license-terms`).
- Maintenance: frequent changelog through v0.195.0 on 2026-08-13 (`claim-factory-droids-sf-maintenance`).
- Lock-in: marketing claims no vendor lock-in via model choice; BYOK is documented as CLI-only, so web/mobile stay on Factory-managed models (`claim-factory-droids-sf-lock-in`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-byok-cli-only`).

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: unknown. First-party sources do not establish a fork or wrapper lineage.
- Relationship edges: unknown. No first-party directed edge to another Battle Harnesses project id was added. Claude Code plugin/agent import is a compatibility feature of Droids, not a `built_on` or `wraps_cli` edge (`claim-factory-droids-sf-plugins`).

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: inferred one Droid runtime across CLI, desktop, web, Slack, IDEs, and persistent Droid Computers, with Missions orchestration (`claim-factory-droids-sf-unique-value`).
- Meaningful drawbacks: BYOK custom models do not appear on web or mobile; OS sandbox is opt-in rather than default (`claim-factory-droids-sf-byok-cli-only`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-isolation`).
- Best fit: individual developers who own a Factory subscription, and review outside a terminal (`claim-factory-droids-sf-intended-user`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-intended-user-review`).
- Not-for: inferred from the CLI-only BYOK surface limit (`claim-factory-droids-sf-not-for`, `claim-factory-droids-sf-byok-cli-only`).
